claim_verdicts.evidence: File read from the tag object (stage-0 -> commit ff911b0): line 1 "# Biên bản họp: chọn cách chặn hủy đơn đã thanh toán"; lines 3-5 "**Mục đích:** …", "**Người dự:** …", "**Thời lượng:** 20 phút."; line 7 is the first section heading "## Quyết định". Three lines, directly under the title, before any heading.

Line 3: "**Mục đích:** quyết định xem đơn `paid` có được hủy hay không." Line 4: "**Người dự:** product owner, hai lập trình viên, tester." = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 attendees. Line 5: "**Thời lượng:** 20 phút." Purpose, four attendees and twenty minutes all match.
Line 7 "## Quyết định"; line 9 is the entire section: "Đơn `paid` **không** hủy được từ ứng dụng. Khách hàng phải yêu cầu hoàn tiền." Exactly two sentences, with the content the claim states.

Lines 13-15: "Hoàn tiền cần đối soát với cổng thanh toán; đội chưa có phần đó. Cho phép hủy mà không hoàn tiền sẽ tạo ra đơn đã hủy nhưng đã thu tiền — trạng thái không ai xử lý được." The file says the refund must be reconciled WITH the payment gateway; it never says "what the gateway recorded", and never says the gateway took the money. The rest of the claim matches.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Under `Lý do` the file gives the reason: a refund has to be reconciled with the payment gateway, the team has not built that part, and cancelling without refunding would leave an order both cancelled and paid — a state nobody handles.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Lines 19-23: header "| Việc | Ai | Khi nào |", separator, then exactly three data rows: "Thêm điều kiện trạng thái vào API hủy | Dev 1 | Trong sprint này", "Ẩn nút \"Hủy đơn\" với đơn `paid` | Dev 2 | Trong sprint này", "Viết story cho luồng hoàn tiền | PO | Trước sprint sau". Row count, columns and assignees match.

Line 23 is the last table row; line 25 is the next heading "## Câu chưa trả lời"; line 27 is its only content: "Đơn `shipped` mà khách từ chối nhận thì tính là gì? PO sẽ hỏi bộ phận vận hành." One unsettled question plus the person who will ask.

Line 31 "## Một bản cập nhật trạng thái ba dòng" is the last section; lines 33-35 are "> Đang làm: …", "> Vướng: … — đã hỏi PO.", "> Tiếp theo: … xong trong hôm nay."; line 37 opens "Ba dòng này thay được một cuộc họp." Three labelled lines, and the file itself calls them a replacement for a meeting.

Lines 37-38, the last sentence in the file: "Nêu vấn đề sớm kèm phương án, đừng nêu muộn kèm lời xin lỗi." (raise the problem early with an option, do not raise it late with an apology). Nothing follows it in the file.

Inputs come from the same file: line 4 lists four attendees (product owner, two developers, tester), line 5 fixes "**Thời lượng:** 20 phút." 4 × 20 min = 80 min > 60 min, and the four sit in the same event, so the time is spent at the same moment. Arithmetic, not opinion.

refs/ has no process mirror (only aspnetcore-docs, docker-docs, dotnet-docs, flutter-website, kubernetes-website, rfc). The one meeting-related source in versions.yaml is the Scrum Guide 2020, which gives "Each event in Scrum is a formal opportunity to inspect and adapt Scrum artifacts" and "Events are used in Scrum to create regularity and to minimize the need for meetings not defined in Scrum" — but no sentence requiring an output or a written record, and none tying the purpose to when a meeting is finished. Normative, undocumented.

The repository file supports only the shape: at stage-0 the note keeps "## Lý do" as its own section under "## Quyết định" (lines 7-15). Neither the Scrum Guide 2020 nor anything in refs/ states that an unwritten decision gets made again, or that the reason is the part a later reader cannot reconstruct. No command can settle it either.

A cost comparison between writing and meeting. Nothing in refs/ or the Scrum Guide 2020 measures it; the nearest sentence, "Daily Scrums improve communications, identify impediments, promote quick decision-making, and consequently eliminate the need for other meetings", is about a Scrum event, not about chat, a story or a pull request description. The lesson's own arithmetic (claim 9) prices the meeting side only.

The file supports the three lines and their replacement value (lines 33-35, 37) and shows the blocked line carrying who was already asked: "> Vướng: chưa rõ đơn `shipped` bị từ chối nhận thì xử lý thế nào — đã hỏi PO." Nothing documents the ranking of the three lines ("usually", "matters when it hands work over") — that is the author's generalisation. Keep what the file shows.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: In the file's three-line update the blocked line names something another person has to clear: `Vướng` records what is unresolved and who has already been asked. The other two say what is being done and what comes next, with a date.

claim_verdicts.evidence: The file shows a reason recorded under `Lý do` (lines 13-15), which supports "a reason, not a preference" as the form the note keeps. The rest — that the team treats the argument as closed once the decision is written, and that reopening it needs something new — is a team norm; no sentence in the Scrum Guide 2020 or in refs/ states it, and no command can settle it.

Claim about what a clarifying question costs a meeting and how often others in the room are unsure. No documentation in refs/; the Scrum Guide 2020 says nothing about who may speak in an event or about the cost of asking. As written ("almost nothing", "often unsure") it is also unfalsifiable.

The early-with-an-option half is the file's own closing rule, lines 37-38 (see claim 8). The rest — that an early problem is a question the team answers and can still change what is built this sprint, while a late one becomes a missed commitment "which is the one that gets discussed" — has no source I can reach: not refs/, not the Scrum Guide 2020.

The last clause is verified by the file: lines 25-27 keep the unsettled question and its owner under "## Câu chưa trả lời". The generalisation before it — that a question nobody wrote down has to be asked again, often in another meeting — has no source in refs/ or the Scrum Guide 2020 and cannot be run.

issues.text: Unlisted claim: the lesson asserts the Đơn Hàng data model in section 2 and then leans on it twice (section 5 "an order both cancelled and paid, a state nobody handles"; section 7 "does it become `cancelled` or a new state"). It is true — db/schema.sql at stage-0 has `status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('new', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'))` — but it is nowhere in the claims ledger, so nothing forces a recheck when the schema moves.
issues.fix: Add a claim of kind `fact`: "At stage-0, db/schema.sql gives orders a single `status` column constrained to 'new', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'", source_hint examples/don-hang db/schema.sql:22-23 at stage-0. The sentence itself can stay as written.
issues.quote: orders in Đơn Hàng carry one named state each, `paid` and `shipped` among them

issues.text: A frequency claim stated as fact and absent from the ledger. Claim 11 covers only "the reason … is the part a later reader cannot reconstruct"; "most often left out" asserts how teams behave across notes in general, which no source in versions.yaml (Scrum Guide 2020 included) supports, and which the one note in the repository contradicts in miniature, since it does record `Lý do` under a heading of its own.
issues.fix: Drop the frequency: "The reason is the part a later reader cannot reconstruct: without it, a new reader has to reopen the argument to get it back." If the emphasis must stay, tie it to the file ("the note gives the reason a heading of its own") and add it to claims.
issues.quote: The reason is the part most often left out and the part a later reader cannot reconstruct

issues.text: The file's line 3 is a statement of what to decide, not a question: "**Mục đích:** quyết định xem đơn `paid` có được hủy hay không." No question mark appears in the three header lines. Section 3 defines the purpose as "the one question a meeting exists to answer", so a reader comparing the two expects a question in the quoted file and does not find one.
issues.fix: Write: "`Mục đích` names what the meeting has to decide: whether a `paid` order may be cancelled." Keep the section 3 sentence as the concept, not as a description of the file.
issues.quote: `Mục đích` states the purpose as a question: may a `paid` order be cancelled or not.

issues.text: Two additions the file does not make. Line 13 says only "Hoàn tiền cần đối soát với cổng thanh toán" — reconcile with the payment gateway. "what the payment gateway recorded" and "the outside service that took the money" are the author's gloss, repeated in the quiz q1 `correct` explanation. Claim 4 carries the same extra wording.
issues.fix: Write: "a refund has to be reconciled with the payment gateway, the outside service the payment goes through". Apply the same change to claim 4 in .meta.json and to the q1 `correct` explanation (en and vi).
issues.quote: a refund has to be matched against what the payment gateway recorded, the outside service that took the money

issues.text: "Payment gateway" is a term I have never met.
